newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Aug gas oil rally slows down.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Aug gas oil rally slows down.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged down at midday on Friday as the market consistently failed to hold on to its gains at above the $23.00-mark as poor fundamentals continued to weigh down on prices, traders said.
"Gas oil is down this morning partly because the market just could not move up to the next level as sellers came out in force every time prices went above $23.00," one trader said.
August was last quoted higher at $22.80/$22.95, down from Thursday's $22.95/$23.05.
September was down five cents at $23.40/$23.55. As a result the August/September spread widened with a trade seen late Thursday at minus 55 cents.
Traders said weaker prices was due to perception among some that the market has peaked in the near time and could come under fresh selling pressure in the physical and swaps market.
The market is looking to the Indian tender to buy September delivery cargoes for fresh indication.

The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade extended its latest rise and was last quoted at $0.40/$0.60. It has widened slightly from Thursday after buying interest emerged in the physical market mid-week.
A U.S. trader bought late on Wednesday a 180,000-barrel and one 150,000-barrel cargoes of jet fuel at $22.60 and $22.50 per barrel respectively for mid-August liftings, free-on-board basis.
August fuel oil was last quoted steady at $101.00/$102.0 per tonne, brokers said.
